kinds.d: Iron or steel bangle worn by Khalsa Sikhs; the circle stands for God as endless.
Small curved sword or knife worn by Khalsa Sikhs as a duty to defend those in peril; the weapon form is in Weapons.
Small wooden comb kept in the hair as a sign of cleanliness.
Cloth draped over the Guru Granth Sahib when it is not being read.
Whisk waved over the Guru Granth Sahib as a sign of respect.
Canopied stand for the Guru Granth Sahib in a home or gurdwara.
Sikh emblem of a double-edged khanda, a chakkar and two crossed kirpans, made as wall plaque, pendant or flag finial.
Jain sacred diagram of nine elements on a lotus, worshipped on brass or silver plates.
